route: kin + -red, perhaps late Old English kinraden
recordText: From *kin* + *-red*, first recorded around 1200, perhaps from a late Old English *kinraden*. The first *d* doesn't belong: it crept in during the 1600s, probably because it's easier to say, perhaps helped along by *kind*. The *kin* in it is Old English *cynn*, family, from *gene-.
gossipText: The family historian. Picked up an extra *d* in the 1600s and will not discuss it.
testimony: There are two stories about him. In one, a king is the leader of the people, meaning our people. In the other, he's from a word for noble birth, a different line entirely. I wrote both down. I underlined neither.
